text:
The scoreboard said MIN 3, NSH 1, and the underlying numbers agreed, which is the less common outcome. MIN generated 3.05 expected goals to NSH's 1.51 and would win 77 percent of simulated replays of every shot. They also outattempted NSH 62 to 46, and the one goal NSH got came on a shot that had a 4 percent chance of going in.

MIN did its damage early. Nick Foligno opened the scoring at 9:35 of the first with a wrist shot, and Blake Coleman made it 2-0 at 13:48 on the power play, one of MIN's four chances with the man advantage. NSH answered once in the second period, when Roman Josi snapped a slap shot past Jesper Wallstedt at 9:23 on that 4 percent look. MIN was the better team in that period too, 0.96 expected goals to 0.38, so the goal said more about luck than about any change in control. Kirill Kaprizov restored the two-goal margin at 4:42 of the third with a tip-in off a Quinn Hughes assist.

Wallstedt finished 19 saves on 20 shots, 0.51 goals saved above expected, while Juuse Saros stopped 27 of 30 and was almost exactly what the shot quality predicted. Hughes logged 27:30 and put five shots on goal. With him on the ice MIN produced 1.6 expected goals against 0.55 allowed. NSH went 0 for 4 on its own power plays, which kept the comeback from ever feeling live.
